_comment: Expected hashes of load-bearing runtime artifacts. This file is DURABLE
SOURCE EVIDENCE and is committed; the artifacts it describes are NOT.
rationale: raw pathology pixels, model binaries and generated databases
must never enter git. But reproducibility requires that a clean clone can
verify what it reconstructs. This file is that anchor: scripts/prepare_runtime.py
recomputes each hash and FAILS on mismatch; scripts/prepare_bake.py copies
only artifacts that pass; the Dockerfile refuses to build without them.
Regenerate deliberately after a model change, and say so in the commit.
Never regenerate to make a verification pass.

database.description: Frozen read model: source_qc (1,144) + immutable predictions (1,144)
_revision_note: HISTORY OF THIS HASH
705ce5c5...  the original frozen read model: schema 0001, 1,144 source_qc
rows, 1,144 predictions, 0 review events, no project column.
cb25f476...  schema 0002 applied (project_id columns added) but the backfill
had not yet run; rows were NULL-scoped. This state is NOT
expected and was a bug: the backfill was gated on 'a migration
was applied this call', so a database that had already recorded
the migration skipped it forever.
<current>    schema 0002 applied AND the 2,288 pre-existing rows backfilled to
project_id='__default__'.
WHY THE HASH CHANGED AND WHY THAT IS SAFE
The migration is additive only: ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN (which SQLite
performs as a schema change without rewriting rows) plus CREATE INDEX. There
is no UPDATE, DELETE, DROP or INSERT against `prediction` anywhere in
0002_project_scope.sql. The backfill's only UPDATE sets project_id on rows
where it IS NULL.
Verified after applying: 1,144 predictions, 0 review events, all still keyed
to model_bundle_hash 01727fb8... ('baseline-frozen-g4') — the original hash is
never reassigned. Scores are untouched; their sums deviate from 1.0 by at
most 1.38e-07, which is one float32 epsilon and reflects how they were
originally stored, not damage.
The database hash is a MIGRATION marker, not a content guarantee. Prediction
integrity is proven by test_migration_is_additive_and_preserves_predictions,
which asserts a prediction row is byte-identical across the migration.
